resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia ties the 1912 renaming to a fire tower in Croghan. The NHLR page's note describes a different Bald Mountain tower near Old Forge that was removed after its ownership changed around 1975. Other sources describe the restored Rondaxe tower as standing. The story reports the disagreement without settling it.
Road Trip Warriors says the tower was built in 1917. NHLR and Masterpieces give a wooden tower in 1912 and the steel tower in 1917. The 1917 date is read as the steel tower.
The brief's 716 m (NHLR) matches the Adirondack Explorer's 2,350 ft. Wikipedia gives 2,313 ft (705 m). The brief's value is kept.

notes_for_editor: The 35 ft height is the NHLR figure and the only height found; the LS-40 model name is not explained in any source read, so height_m 10.7 is unverified. The NHLR note describing a removed Bald Mountain tower near Old Forge conflicts with the other sources and needs an editor's check. The NHLR claim that the tower is on the National Register is unverified; NPGallery was not read. Andy Arthur pages returned HTTP 403 and were not used. The 15,000-visitor figure is from Wikipedia alone, and the 'more than 30 observers' figure is from a blog. Adirondack Explorer does not give a date for its article.
